content: When the bridge shells out to a provider CLI, treat its argument contract as unversioned and probe the real installed binary with a fail-fast input (a bogus --model) whenever a review path fails with a parse-shaped error. Order flags so any value-consuming flag (--print, --prompt) is LAST with its value, never followed by another flag.
context: agy 1.1.27 changed --print from "read the prompt on stdin" to "the next argument IS the prompt". Our argv `--print --sandbox --model …` then handed "--sandbox" to agy as the prompt, so every Gemini review failed — and because Gemini only runs as failover when Codex is rate-limited, a two-provider setup silently became zero-provider exactly when it mattered. A peer node lost review coverage for a multi-day landing and found two MAJORs by hand. Reproduced with the exact error text, fixed in 63fbe12 by making the prompt the final argv value plus a 120 KiB guard (Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN).
title: Provider CLIs change their argument contracts silently; probe the real binary, don't trust the last known shape
